observations: What I read for this request: the new first-reading section (fingerprint 3fdb956f..., firstReadingHash e4fbf194e936ac0d0464bb79ed643d9fb94a2ea4a18eaa61ffdbbd3ce2d2fc6d). The rest of the page 08 script, source/original.txt and REVISION-2026-11-11.md (Request 4) I had read earlier in this session. In this pass I opened workflow/review/page-08.png, assets/panels/08-2.png and assets/panels/08-6.png with Read and looked at them. Earlier in this session I had looked at assets/panels/08-1.png, 08-3.png and 08-5.png. I did not open the panel art for 08-4, storyboards/page-08.svg or the pharmacy-lab character sheet.
All captions, labels and the lab technician's line match source PAGE 8 word for word. Nothing names a drug, a test, a value or a diagnosis.

08-5, the change: the RESULTS READY box now spans about x 448-618. Dr. Ananya's tablet-holding hand (protected [631,1075,40,56]; about x 632 in the art, scaled about 0.40) sits about 13 px to the right. Her fingers, the tablet's left edge and the tube-and-check card are all fully visible. This resolves the earlier contact, which the first reader also noted as 'close but not overlapping'.

08-1: NEW PRESCRIPTION now sits directly above the tablet. Its bottom edge meets the tablet's top bezel, but the pill card on the screen is fully visible, and the label works as the tablet's own heading. The caption box ends at about x 286, about 5 px left of the pharmacist's hair (which starts at about x 291 in the art). His face, his hand and the box he is putting into the bag (protected [265,214,95,50]) are clear. Acceptable.

08-2: the caption 'The lab is / notified.' sits at the top-right border, with LAB ORDER below it. The label's bottom meets the monitor's top bezel. The three tube icons and the order card on the screen stay visible (they sit in the lower middle of the screen in the 08-2 art). Her face, bun, glasses and raised tube are left of the label, which starts at about x 786. Acceptable.

08-3, tail and bun: the tail leaves the balloon's lower-left corner and ends at the right side of the lab technician's head, near her bun. The balloon corner sits just above and to the right of the bun without covering it. Ravi is about 350 px away on the left, so the tail can only belong to her. Acceptable.

08-6: RESULTS READY covers the top bezel and the upper-left plain area of the monitor. The check card (about y 1295-1350) is visible, and Meera's face (x 710-790), hair and braid are clear (the 08-6 art shows the check card in the middle of the screen, below the label). Acceptable.

Text fit (first-reader point 6): 'fills' in 08-1 has about 6 px of right padding, against about 18 px on the left. 'his' in 08-3, 'on' in 08-5 and 'ready.' in the balloon sit near their borders, but every glyph is fully inside its box and legible. These are tight, but not defects.

Typography (point 7): the gap in 'We' ll' comes from the monospace font. The same apostrophe appears throughout the comic ('We'll' on 06, 'Let's' and 'That's' on 07, 'I've' on 05), so it is consistent house lettering and readable. Ending a line after a middle dot ('app ·') follows the same pattern as the labels on pages 05-06 ('prescribing ·', 'current vitals ·'). The apparent indent on 'is notified' in 08-5 and 08-6 is the narrow, centred monospace 'i', not a leading space (the textColumns have trailing spaces only).

Tube caps (point 8): the 08-2 art shows purple caps and the 08-3 art shows red caps, both on the tube she holds and on the rack. This is an artwork matter, not lettering. No text names a colour or claims it is the same tube. In a clinic lab, different tests use tubes with different coloured caps, so the mismatch reads as plausible and does not change the meaning. I do not count it as a lettering issue. The parent may pass it to an artwork review if exact prop continuity is wanted.

Unnamed woman in 08-6 (point 9): the first reader saw page 08 alone. In the comic, pages 01-07 have established Meera at this reception desk, in this blue kurta with this braid. The caption refers to 'the clinic' on purpose, because the notification goes to the clinic through Welbuk Practice. Acceptable.

Timeline against pages 06-07: 07-4 shows Ravi walking away from the clinic. 'Meanwhile' reads as 'while he heads off'. 'Later that day, Ravi gives his samples at the clinic lab', with his bag on his lap, shows he came back the same day, which is the decision confirmed in Request 4. The 06-2 label 'intelligent prescribing · ... · labs' sets up NEW PRESCRIPTION and LAB ORDER. 08-4's 'Results ready' and its evening setting at home mark a later day.

Reading the page cold: top row left to right; the wide middle panel, caption at top left and then the balloon at top right; then the tall bottom-left panel, caption and then label; then the two stacked right panels, top to bottom. In every panel the white caption sits above or to the left of the teal label, so each panel reads caption first, then label.
The only speech is in 08-3, and it shares that row only with its own caption, so a skip is unlikely. The two RESULTS READY labels sit in separate panels.

Two notifications side by side in the top row, pharmacy then lab, with matching 'is notified' captions and on-screen labels.
Same lab, same technician, now in a wide shot. 'Later that day' and Ravi in the collection chair with a cotton pad show that he came back.
Her promise 'We'll let you know when your results are ready' leads directly into 'Results ready: Ravi is notified.' at home in evening light.
The same 'is notified' pattern moves on to Dr. Ananya, at her desk and in the clothes from pages 05-06.
Stacked panels with matching captions: the doctor on Welbuk Care, then the clinic on Welbuk Practice, both showing the same check card.

With the chain of notifications complete, the caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' and the train window open a clearly marked, conditional jump into the future on the vision page the user kept.

readingReview.comparison: The order in the new first reading matches the intended order for 08-1 to 08-6, caption before label in every panel, and nothing was skipped. I judged each of its points against the art: the tail and balloon corner near the bun, the labels meeting prop bezels in 08-1, 08-2 and 08-6, the caption near the pharmacist's hair, and the 08-5 label (now about 13 px clear of the hand). None hides a face, hand or key screen content. The tight text is fully inside its boxes. The apostrophe spacing and the line ending after a middle dot are consistent house style. The difference in cap colour is a plausible artwork variation with no text depending on it. The unnamed woman is Meera, established on pages 01-07. Read alongside page 07, the timeline is clear.
